name: Dead hang

technique.setup: Stand on a box under the bar and take an overhand grip just wider than the shoulders. Lift the feet off the box to hang, and step back onto it to finish.
cues: Wrap the thumbs around the bar and squeeze
Let the arms go fully straight
Keep the ribs down and legs together
Breathe slowly through the hold
mistakes: Dropping off the bar instead of stepping down to the box
Swinging or kicking the legs
Holding the breath
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder or elbow
Pinching at the front or top of the shoulder
Numbness or tingling in the hands or fingers

media.searchHint: Hybrid Calisthenics dead hang how to and benefits

notes: Journal dose: 60 s or max time x3. Start where the hold feels controlled and build towards 60 s.

name: Active hang

technique.setup: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip just wider than the shoulders, starting from a box. Keep the arms straight the whole time.
cues: Pull the shoulders down away from the ears
Keep the arms straight, don't bend the elbows
Squeeze the glutes and keep the legs together
mistakes: Bending the elbows to fake the shoulder pull
Arching the lower back to lift the chest
Shrugging back up during the hold
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Numbness or tingling in the hands

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs active hang scapula depression tutorial

notes: Marchon uses 20 s active hangs in supersets.

technique.setup: Start from a box and hang from the bar with straight arms, overhand grip just wider than the shoulders.
cues: Pull the shoulders down and slightly back
Keep the elbows straight, the body rises a few centimetres
Pause one second at the top, then lower slowly to a full hang
mistakes: Bending the elbows and turning it into a small pull-up
Swinging to get the body up
Rushing the lowering
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder
Pinching or clicking pain at the front of the shoulder
Numbness or tingling in the hands

name: TRX row

technique.setup: Hold the handles and walk the feet forward until the arms are straight and the body leans back. The more upright you stand, the easier it is: start steep, then walk the feet forward to make it harder.
cues: Body in one line, squeeze glutes
Pull the shoulders back first, then drive the elbows back
Handles to the bottom of the ribs
Lower slowly to straight arms
mistakes: Hips sagging during the pull
Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
Half reps that stop before straight arms
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder or elbow
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

notes: Log the angle as steep, medium or flat (body close to horizontal). Hitting 4x12 at one angle moves to the next flatter angle.

name: Band row

technique.setup: Anchor the band in a closed door at chest height. Hold both ends, step back until the band is taut with straight arms, and stand tall with soft knees.
cues: Shoulders down and back before the arms move
Drive the elbows back past the ribs
Squeeze the shoulder blades for one second
Return slowly against the band
mistakes: Leaning back to pull with the body
Shrugging the shoulders up
Letting the band snap the arms forward
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
The door or anchor shifting

media.searchHint: Calisthenicmovement resistance band row door anchor at home

notes: Close the door towards you so the anchor pulls the door shut, not open. Hitting 3x15 moves to the next heavier band.

name: Inverted row

technique.setup: Set a bar at about hip height. Lie under it, grip just wider than the shoulders, and straighten the body with heels on the floor (bend the knees to make it easier, raise the feet to make it harder).
cues: Body in one line, squeeze glutes
Pull the chest to the bar, elbows about 45 degrees
Pause with the chest at the bar
Lower slowly to straight arms
mistakes: Hips sagging or piking up
Reaching the chin to the bar instead of the chest
Elbows flared straight out to the sides
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder or elbow
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

notes: Journal: 10-12 x3-4, feet elevated; a variant holds the chest at the bar for 3 s each rep (8x4, p09). Log foot elevation as floor, box or bench.

name: Pull-up slow negative

technique.setup: Stand on a box high enough that you can step up into the top position with the chin over the bar. Lower yourself, then step back down onto the box: never drop from a full hang.
cues: Start chin over the bar, shoulders down
Lower for 3-5 seconds, counting out loud
Keep tension all the way to straight arms
Step back onto the box to reset
mistakes: Dropping fast through the bottom half
Jumping up and dropping off the bar
Shrugging the shoulders to the ears at the bottom
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
You can no longer control a 3-second lowering

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs negative pull ups eccentric tutorial

notes: Works with either grip (chin-up grip is often easier). Stop the set when a rep drops faster than 3 s.

name: Band-assisted pull-up

technique.setup: Loop the band over the bar and step one foot (or both knees) into it from a box. Grip just wider than the shoulders and hang with straight arms.
cues: Pull the shoulders down first
Drive the elbows to the ribs
Chin over the bar, then lower slowly
Ribs down, legs together
mistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Half reps that stop before straight arms
Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
The band slipping off the foot

notes: Hitting 4x10 moves to the next lighter band. Step out of the band onto the box at the end of the set.

name: Strict pull-up

technique.setup: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip just wider than the shoulders, arms straight and legs together. Use a box to reach the bar and to step down after the set.
cues: Pull the shoulders down before bending the arms
Drive the elbows down to the ribs
Chin clearly over the bar
Lower under control to straight arms
mistakes: Kicking or swinging (kipping) to get up
Half reps that stop before straight arms
Craning the neck to get the chin over
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Numbness or tingling in the hands

notes: Journal formats: 8x4, 5x4 per grip (wide, normal, close), 5 min EMOM with the same reps each minute.

name: Chin-up

technique.setup: Hang from the bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms straight. Use a box to reach the bar and to step down after the set.
cues: Shoulders down, chest up
Pull the elbows down and in to the ribs
Chin over the bar, then lower slowly
Keep the wrists straight, not bent back
mistakes: Swinging or kicking to get up
Stopping short of straight arms at the bottom
Gripping so narrow the elbows and wrists twist
stopIf: Pain on the inside of the elbow or the front of the forearm
Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder or wrist
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

notes: Journal variant: 5 s hold at the top plus a 3 s lowering. Underhand grip stresses the inner elbow more; switch to pull-ups if that area gets sore.

name: Chest-to-bar pull-up

technique.setup: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip just wider than the shoulders, legs together and slightly forward of the bar.
cues: Pull the shoulders down and back hard
Drive the elbows down behind the body
Touch the upper chest to the bar
Lower slowly to straight arms
mistakes: Kipping or swinging to reach the bar
Only reaching chin height
Flaring the ribs to fake the height
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder or elbow
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs chest to bar pull up tutorial

notes: Part of the muscle-up gate.

name: Explosive pull-up

technique.setup: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip just wider than the shoulders, arms straight and body still. Do these fresh, early in the session.
cues: Start from a dead stop, no swing
Pull as fast as possible, chest towards the bar
Keep the hands on the bar
Lower slowly to straight arms
mistakes: Kipping or swinging to create speed
Letting go of the bar before the technique is solid
Grinding slow reps when tired instead of ending the set
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder or elbow
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Reps visibly slowing down

notes: Quality over quantity: end the set as soon as a rep is slower than the first.

name: High pull-up

technique.setup: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width, legs together and slightly in front of the bar. Do these fresh, early in the session.
cues: Pull explosively, driving the bar towards the hips
Lean the shoulders back as you rise
Keep the legs together and the body tight
Lower slowly to straight arms
mistakes: Kicking the legs to get height
Pulling straight up instead of pulling the bar towards the hips
Doing them when tired at the end of a session
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder or elbow
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Wrist pain from the grip rolling over the bar

media.searchHint: Calisthenicmovement high pull ups muscle up progression

notes: First step of the muscle-up tree; only after the muscle-up gate (8-10 strict pull-ups, 10 dips, chest-to-bar).

name: Archer pull-up

technique.setup: Take a wide overhand grip, about twice shoulder-width, and hang with straight arms and legs together.
cues: Pull towards one hand, that elbow bends to the ribs
Slide the other arm out straight along the bar
Chin over the working hand
Lower slowly to the middle, then switch sides
mistakes: Bending the straight arm so both arms share the work
Swinging or twisting the body
Rushing the lowering
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow of the straight arm
Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder

notes: Journal dose was 8x4 (alternating); start lower. Part of the one-arm pull-up gate.

name: Weighted pull-up

technique.setup: Hold a light dumbbell between the feet (or use a dip belt) while standing on a box, then take an overhand grip just wider than the shoulders. Step back onto the box after the last rep.
cues: Squeeze the weight tight with the feet
Shoulders down, then elbows to the ribs
Chin clearly over the bar
Lower under control to straight arms
mistakes: Adding weight before 3x8 strict bodyweight reps
Swinging the weight to get up
Dropping off the bar with the weight attached
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
The weight starting to slip

notes: Journal used a 5 min EMOM. Hitting 3x8 moves to the next weight up.

technique.setup: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip just wider than the shoulders and lift straight legs to hip height (bend the knees into a tuck if needed). Late progression: only once strict pull-ups and an L-sit hold are solid.
cues: Lift the legs first and keep them still
Shoulders down, then pull the elbows to the ribs
Chin over the bar without the legs dropping
Lower slowly to straight arms
mistakes: Legs dropping or swinging during the pull
Rounding forward and losing the shoulder position
Half reps at the bottom
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder or elbow
Pinching at the front of the shoulder
Cramping or sharp pain at the front of the hip

name: Band straight-arm pulldown

technique.setup: Anchor the band at the top of a closed door. Hold the ends with straight arms in front at head height, step back until taut and hinge slightly forward.
cues: Shoulders down away from the ears
Sweep the straight arms down to the thighs
Ribs down, don't arch the back
Return slowly to head height
mistakes: Bending the elbows to turn it into a row
Arching the lower back at the bottom
Letting the band pull the arms up fast
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder
Pinching at the front or top of the shoulder
The door or anchor shifting

media.searchHint: Calisthenicmovement resistance band straight arm pulldown lats

notes: Home stand-in for hangs and pull-up work: trains the lats and shoulder pull-down without a bar.

name: One-arm dumbbell row

technique.setup: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a bench, other foot on the floor, back flat. Hold the dumbbell with the free arm hanging straight.
cues: Back flat, neck long
Pull the elbow back towards the hip
Squeeze the shoulder blade at the top
Lower slowly to a full stretch
mistakes: Twisting the torso to swing the weight up
Rounding the back
Shrugging the shoulder to the ear
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the elbow or shoulder
Sharp pain in the lower back

notes: Hitting 3x12 per side moves to the next weight up.

name: Band face pull

technique.setup: Anchor a light band in a closed door at face height. Hold the ends with palms facing down, step back until taut and stand tall.
cues: Pull the hands towards the forehead, elbows high
Rotate the hands back so the fists end beside the ears
Squeeze the upper back for one second
Return slowly
mistakes: Using a band so heavy the lower back arches
Dropping the elbows into a row
Shrugging the shoulders up
stopIf: Pinching at the front or top of the shoulder
Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder or elbow

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs resistance band face pull shoulder health

notes: Light shoulder-health work; the journal pairs it with dips (15x3).

name: Band pull-apart

technique.setup: Hold a light band in front of the chest with straight arms, hands shoulder-width apart, palms down.
cues: Ribs down, stand tall
Pull the band apart until it touches the chest
Keep the arms straight and the shoulders down
Return slowly
mistakes: Bending the elbows to make it easier
Arching the lower back
Shrugging the shoulders up
stopIf: Pinching at the front or top of the shoulder
Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder

notes: Warm-up staple before pull or push days.

name: IYT raise

technique.setup: Lie face down on the floor, forehead on a folded towel, arms straight. Bodyweight is enough to start; very light dumbbells (0.5-2 kg) are optional.
cues: Thumbs up, shoulders down away from the ears
Lift the arms in an I (overhead), then a Y, then a T
Lift from the shoulder blades, not the lower back
Pause one second at the top of each letter
mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift higher
Shrugging the shoulders
Using weights heavy enough to swing
stopIf: Pinching at the top or front of the shoulder, especially in the I and Y
Sharp or joint pain in the shoulder

media.searchHint: Antranik prone Y T I raises scapular strength

notes: Reps count per letter: journal used 15 each x3. Can also be done bent over with a band or prone on a bench.

name: Dumbbell curl

technique.setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight by the sides and palms forward (palms in for hammer curls).
cues: Elbows pinned to the sides
Curl up without swinging the body
Squeeze at the top, then lower for 2-3 seconds
mistakes: Swinging the hips to lift the weight
Elbows drifting forward
Dropping the weight on the way down
stopIf: Sharp pain in the elbow or the front of the forearm
Sharp or joint pain in the wrist

notes: Journal variant: 10 curls plus a 10 s hammer hold at 90 degrees. Hitting 3x12 moves to the next weight up.

name: Band curl

technique.setup: Stand on the middle of the band with feet hip-width apart and hold the ends, arms straight by the sides, palms forward.
cues: Elbows pinned to the sides
Curl up without leaning back
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly against the band
mistakes: Leaning back to finish the rep
Elbows drifting forward
Letting the band snap the hands down
stopIf: Sharp pain in the elbow or the front of the forearm
Sharp or joint pain in the wrist
The band slipping from under the feet

media.searchHint: Calisthenicmovement resistance band biceps curl at home

notes: Hitting 3x15 moves to the next heavier band.
